item.title: BGVD-State: Replayable middleware for evidence-gated handoffs in third-party software security review
item.description: Third-party software security review is iterative: models, tools, and people raise suspected-risk candidates, test them against evidence, and hand the evolving review state to subsequent reviewers. Conversation logs preserve observations but may lose track of which candidates remain active, which evidence is current, which paths failed, and which decision controls reporting. item.title: YB_Mol Studio: an agent-integrated visual editing platform for molecular and materials design
item.description: Molecular and materials design requires researchers to inspect structures, edit molecular objects and connect each change to computation. Artificial intelligence (AI) agents add another operating mode: they need executable molecular operations, visible intermediate states and a way to continue from prior results. item.title: Cost-Effective Repository Exploration for Agentic Issue Localization
item.description: Repository exploration is a distinct and costly stage of coding-agent pipelines: before generating a patch, an agent must identify which repository files are likely to matter. We study whether this stage can be delegated to lower-cost models while retaining useful localization quality. item.description: Abstract Highway ramp merging areas are critical bottlenecks affecting traffic safety and operational efficiency, where interactions between mainline and ramp vehicles often induce traffic conflicts, crashes, and delays. item.title: Parallel science and technology for C2 in the agentic age: from military operations to peaceful sustainability and resiliency
item.description: Abstract Command and control (C2) has traditionally been framed as a military problem of sensing, deciding, coordinating, and acting under uncertainty, conflict, and time pressure. item.title: SAGE: Source-Aligned Governance for Human–Agent Requirements Clarification in Multi-agent Software Engineering
item.description: Multi-agent large language model workflows are increasingly used in software engineering, yet requirements clarification under human–agent collaboration remains weakly governed. Much of the rework reflects requirement-chain desynchronization: negotiated intent, workflow contracts, and signed deliverables evolve on separate tracks without auditable linkage, yielding semantic drift and unclear accountability. item.title: Decompose to Conquer: A Multi-agent LLM Pipeline for Requirements Engineering and Software Design
item.description: The automation of Requirements Engineering (RE) and software design using Large Language Models (LLMs) remains an open challenge, particularly in capturing stakeholders’ intent accurately and fully for complex real-world software. item.title: Specifying the Delegated-Autonomy Boundary: Requirements Engineering for Agentic AI
item.description: Agentic AI systems do not just predict or recommend; they plan, maintain state, and act in external environments with varying degrees of autonomy. item.title: An AI assisted four layer teaching model for computational thinking cultivation evaluated in a 14 week classroom pilot
item.description: Computational thinking has become a foundational competency for 21st-century learners, yet effective and scalable approaches to its cultivation remain insufficient. This study addresses three persistent gaps in the literature: the lack of systematically integrated AI-assisted pedagogical architectures, the inadequate operationalization of personalized learning paths for computational thinking, and the reliance on single-dimensional evaluation metrics. item.title: How does explicit reliability guide choices? Effect of trustworthiness on choice and metacognition
item.description: A key challenge in today's fast-paced digital world is to integrate information from various sources, which differ in their reliability. Yet, little is known about how explicit probabilistic information about the likelihood that a source provides correct information is used in decision-making. Here, we investigated how such explicit reliability markers are integrated into decisions and the extent to which individuals have metacognitive insight into this process. item.title: The impact of artificial intelligence on students’ metacognition: a systematic review
item.description: Given the critical role of metacognition in academic achievement and the rapid integration of Artificial Intelligence (AI) in educational settings, understanding the interplay between the two has become essential. In recent years, a growing number of studies have examined their relationship, creating a pressing need for a systematic review to synthesize the accumulating evidence.
